asymptotic_endpoint.statement: No finite bijective YBE solution is simultaneously a rigid core and asymptotically rack-invisible, i.e. satisfies forall m forall N exists n>N with N_{m,n}(X) != 1.
asymptotic_endpoint.strictly_smaller_than_rigid_core_exclusi: Rigid-looking cores whose rack-prefix pressure is bounded in arity no longer need to be excluded separately, because fixed-arity cofinality would patch the bounded arities.
asymptotic_endpoint.why_it_implies_sawin_yes: A minimal Sawin counterexample must avoid all settled positive branches, hence must be rigid. Fixed-arity rack cofinality then forces its obstruction to be unbounded in arity. Excluding asymptotically rack-invisible rigid cores excludes minimal counterexamples.

fixed_arity_theorem.consequence_for_ybe: For every finite YBE solution X and every fixed arity n, some finite rack Y_n satisfies ker rho^{Y_n}_n <= ker rho^X_n.
fixed_arity_theorem.detector: Y is the conjugation rack of G=F_n/K, where K is the characteristic finite-index subgroup supplied by the Artin congruence subgroup property.
proof_steps: Let N=ker theta. Since H is finite, N has finite index in B_n.
Choose characteristic finite-index K <= F_n with C_G=ker(B_n -> Aut(F_n/K)) <= N.
Set G=F_n/K and give G the conjugation rack operation a*b=aba^{-1}.
Under the standard Artin convention sigma_i sends (x_i,x_{i+1}) to (x_i x_{i+1} x_i^{-1}, x_i), which is exactly the conjugation rack crossing on the tuple of quotient generators.
If beta is trivial on the rack action on G^n, it fixes every tuple, in particular the tuple of quotient free generators.
Those quotient generators generate G, so beta is trivial in Aut(G), hence beta lies in C_G <= N.
fixed_arity_theorem.statement: Fix n >= 2. For every finite quotient representation theta:B_n -> H, there is a finite rack Y such that ker rho^Y_n <= ker theta.

literature_input.name: Artin congruence subgroup property for braid groups
literature_input.statement: For the Artin embedding B_n -> Aut(F_n), every finite-index subgroup of B_n contains a principal congruence kernel ker(B_n -> Aut(F_n/K)) for some characteristic finite-index subgroup K <= F_n.
literature_input.status: Used as external literature input; Stylianakis records this form as Asada's theorem and notes Thurston's elementary proof.

sharpened_negative_condition.new_condition: forall m forall N exists n>N with N_{m,n}(X) != 1
sharpened_negative_condition.old_condition: forall m exists n with N_{m,n}(X) != 1
proof: Let P be a finite product of racks.
If P dominates X in all arities above N_0, use fixed-arity cofinality to choose racks Q_n for the bounded arities 2 <= n <= N_0.
Then Y=P x product_{2 <= n <= N_0} Q_n is a finite rack dominating X in every arity.
Therefore a genuinely non-dominated X must have rack-prefix pressure above every finite arity cutoff.

singular_coordinate_filter.finite_table_filter: A rigid-core search can reject any nonterminal candidate with at least one bijective left coordinate map or at least one bijective right coordinate map.
proof_steps: The first YBE component identity gives L_{L_x(y)} L_{R_y(x)} = L_x L_y.
If x,y in U_L, the right side is bijective; over a finite set both left-side factors are bijective.
Thus r(U_L^2) is contained in U_L^2, and bijectivity of r makes this equality.
So U_L is empty, all of X, or a proper crossing-closed subsolution.
The left-nondegenerate branch excludes U_L=X, and the no-proper-subsolution rigid-core condition excludes nonempty proper U_L.
The same argument using R_z R_y = R_{R_z(y)} R_{L_y(z)} gives the right-coordinate conclusion.
singular_coordinate_filter.statement: A minimal counterexample outside the left/right-nondegenerate branches and with no proper crossing-closed subsolution has every L_x and every R_x non-bijective.
